answer: verified. I ran `checks/settle-repro.sh` against each of the 10 commits, extracted with `git archive`. It passes at `36f883f` through `a16f8ab` and fails at `91a6a15` and every later commit. `91a6a15` is "ledger: tidy settle loop", and its parent `a16f8ab` passes, so it is the first failing commit. I changed no files.

`interlock check run --criterion answer` reported there is no check to run for this criterion, so I recorded the per-commit runs as an `observed` assessment.

checks_run: for c in $(git log --format=%h); do d=$(mktemp -d); git archive $c | tar -x -C $d; printf "%s " $c; (cd $d && sh $OLDPWD/checks/settle-repro.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo pass || echo FAIL); rm -rf $d; done; git status --short
git show 91a6a15 --stat --format=%H | head; interlock check run --criterion answer 2>&1 | tail -5

interlock claim add --criterion answer --strength observed --tree auto --ref "for each commit: git archive | tar -x tmp; sh checks/settle-repro.sh" --note "Repro fails at 91a6a15 and every later commit; passes at its parent a16f8ab and all earlier commits. 91a6a15 changes only tally/ledger.py (tidy settle loop)." 2>&1 | tail -3
git log --format=%H\ %s | head -20; cat checks/settle-repro.sh; interlock check run --criterion answer 2>&1 | tail -5

cp checks/settle-repro.sh /tmp/r.sh; for c in $(git rev-list --reverse 7e2bd53); do d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/v.XXXX); git archive $c | tar -x -C $d; (cd $d && sh /tmp/r.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "$c pass" || echo "$c FAIL"); done; git status --short

interlock assess add --criterion answer --strength observed --ref "git archive each commit; sh checks/settle-repro.sh" --note "Ran repro on all 10 commits: pass at 36f883f..a16f8ab, fail at 91a6a15 and all later. 91a6a15 is first failing; parent a16f8ab passes. No files changed."
